ra: Ali as the Ma'na (Ayn) is the first member of the Ayn-Mim-Sin triad (Friedman 2010; Bar-Asher & Kofsky 2002).
Muhammad as the Ism (Mim) is the second member of the Ayn-Mim-Sin triad.
Salman as the Bab (Sin) is the third member of the Ayn-Mim-Sin triad.
In Nusayri doctrine Ali is the manifestation/embodiment of the divine Ma'na (Meaning), the supreme essence (Halm 1982).
Muhammad embodies al-Ism, the Name/veil, in the Muhammadan cycle (Halm 1982).
Salman embodies al-Bab, the Gate, in the Muhammadan cycle (Halm 1982).
Nusayri emanationist cosmology: the Name (Ism) is emanated from the Meaning (Ma'na) (Bar-Asher & Kofsky 2002).
The Gate (Bab) is emanated from the Name (Ism), completing the descending triad (Bar-Asher & Kofsky 2002).
The five Aytam are attested as emanated below the Bab in the Nusayri cosmic hierarchy (Bar-Asher & Kofsky 2002).
The Ayn-Mim-Sin formula is the creedal expression that names and symbolizes the divine triad (Bar-Asher & Kofsky 2002).
The Ali-Muhammad-Salman triad constitutes the final (Muhammadan) cycle within the doctrine of seven cycles of manifestation (Halm 1982).
Ibn Nusayr al-Namiri is the founder-prophet credited with proclaiming the deification of Ali and the trinitarian doctrine (Friedman 2010).

Ibn Nusayr claimed to be the Bab (Gate) of the Imams Ali al-Hadi and Hasan al-Askari, occupying/embodying the Bab office in his own age (Friedman 2010). [QA: verb changed from member_of to embodies — an entity cannot be member_of a divine principle.]
Al-Khasibi stands in the doctrinal lineage descending from Ibn Nusayr, whose teaching he systematized and organized (Friedman 2010).
Al-Khasibi systematized and transmitted Nusayri cosmology including the cyclical-manifestation doctrine in his Kitab al-Hidaya al-Kubra (Bar-Asher & Kofsky 2002).

The Alawite deified Ali (Ma'na) is a sectarian reception of the same historical Ali ibn Abi Talib venerated in mainstream/Twelver Shi'ism as first Imam (homonym, same person, divergent theology; Friedman 2010).
The Alawite Muhammad (Ism/veil) is a sectarian reception of the Prophet Muhammad, here theologically subordinated to Ali (homonym, same person; Friedman 2010).
The Alawite Salman (Bab/Gate) is a sectarian reception of the Companion Salman al-Farisi, elevated to the third hypostasis of the triad (homonym, same person; Friedman 2010).
Ibn Nusayr is historically associated as a disciple/claimed Bab of the eleventh Imam Hasan al-Askari, linking the sect's origin to the Twelver Imami line (Friedman 2010).
The Alawite cyclical-manifestation doctrine develops out of and radicalizes the Shi'i doctrine of Imamah / divinely-guided guidance (Halm 1982).
